text: Encourage choosing one skill to practice simply because getting better feels satisfying.
Encourage questions that begin with why, how, or what if.
Encourage hobbies that involve making, building, performing, collecting, or investigating.
Encourage reading beyond assigned school material.
Encourage explaining how they solved something rather than only showing the answer.
Encourage helping with a real household task from start to finish.
Encourage trying a second strategy when the first one fails.
Encourage cooperative games where the goal depends on the group.
Encourage active play that develops a broad range of movement skills.
Encourage keeping a small record of progress on a personally meaningful project.
Encourage asking for feedback from a teacher, coach, or other trusted adult.
Encourage noticing another person's perspective during disagreements.
Encourage creative work that has no requirement to be displayed or judged.
Encourage making plans for a small project and adjusting them as reality changes.
Encourage healthy digital habits that leave room for sleep, movement, people, and hobbies.
Encourage trying unfamiliar foods without requiring a child to finish them.
Encourage participation in community, school, cultural, or recreational activities that fit the child.
Encourage leadership in small, real responsibilities rather than performative titles.
Encourage celebrating improvement as well as outcomes.
Encourage curiosity about how everyday objects and systems work.
Encourage repairing or reusing things when practical.
Encourage kind disagreement and respectful debate.
Encourage independent preparation for recurring routines.
Encourage returning to a difficult skill after a reasonable break.
Encourage sharing expertise with others without making expertise a status contest.
